races.name: CopyBet BOG Now For York Tomorrow Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Smugglers Haven
runners_data.note: Uncontested front-runner with two wins over similar trips on good ground this season, ridden by the claiming conditionals jockey Miss Lily Bradstock; 43 days since last run is not a concern given trainer Sara Bradstock's patient approach, and her sim-going record of 4 wins from 9 underlines her suitability for today's conditions.
runners_data.comment: Smugglers Haven has winning form at today's distance and going, and her recent record of two wins in her last five starts — including a victory two starts back — marks her as the one to beat here, with 43 days between runs the only minor query.

runners_data.name: Palamon
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's yard is in decent form (2/5 in 14 days) but Palamon's personal record of 1 win from 15 similar-going runs is modest; a hold-up horse at heart, he faces the structural problem that several rivals ahead of him in the map are also not natural front-runners, squeezing the space he needs to finish off races.
runners_data.comment: Palamon shaped with real promise when third two starts back, and his going experience holds him in good stead off a 120 mark; the worry is that his latest fifth suggests he may need to recapture that form.

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners a horse in excellent recent form — four places from four on good ground — and the bp headgear suggests he concentrates best when ridden prominently; his two wins at 23-26f on good ground are directly relevant to today's test and he is the most likely beneficiary if Smugglers Haven weakens late.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, Muskerry Rock faces a stiff ask under 166 lb, yet his recent form is genuinely solid — two wins and two seconds in his last four starts — and he has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: King Roly
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a messy recent form string (46-P29) that includes a pulled-up effort; the tb headgear has been tried without dramatic improvement, and his sim-going record of 3 wins from 15 reflects inconsistency rather than class — he needs a lot to go wrong ahead of him.
runners_data.comment: King Roly shaped with promise when second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 127 marking him as a strong threat; the risk is he pulled up three starts back, and remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Harrys Hope
runners_data.note: Solid placed record on good ground (3 wins, 8 places from 15 similar-going runs) but his natural style is hold-up, and with Yes Day also a genuine back-marker, he is mapped to midfield against his instincts; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that racing out of role tempers his chance, even if his raw form is competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Harrys Hope faces a stiff ask at 157 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a second two starts back shows she retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Yes Day
runners_data.note: Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim helps offset a tricky draw in the weight-for-age structure, and Yes Day's recent form of 2-3-2 shows he is in good nick; however, as a genuine hold-up horse forced to map to midfield alongside Harrys Hope, his chance is similarly conditioned by the style mismatch — his best efforts have come when able to close from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and hitting peak form, Yes Day has finished second, third, and second in his last three starts and returns here after a 32-day break with distance and going experience in his favour; yet to land a win in recent starts is the one concern.

races.paceDynamic: Smugglers Haven is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she will dictate from the front at a pace entirely of her own choosing over 2m7f on good ground at Worcester. Muskerry Rock is the only prominent-style horse and will sit closest in second, creating a small lead group with the remainder strung behind. With Smugglers Haven uncontested and carrying proven course-and-distance form, the tempo will be measured and controlled, making it very hard for hold-up horses to generate the momentum needed to reel her in late. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles — Smugglers Haven and Muskerry Rock are ideally placed structurally, while Harrys Hope and Yes Day, though genuine hold-up types by nature, have been redistributed into the midfield map because there are more hold-up horses than the rear can accommodate, meaning neither is guaranteed to operate in their true comfort zone.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Smugglers Haven controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Smugglers Haven dictates a measured gallop from the front and faces no serious pace challenge throughout.
scenarios.body: She leads from flag to finish at her own rhythm, jumping cleanly and using her proven stamina to grind out the 2m7f trip on good ground; her recent wins at similar trips and her sim-going record of 4 wins from 9 in these conditions underpin her dominance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent challenger swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If Muskerry Rock tracks Smugglers Haven closely and produces a challenge from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: Muskerry Rock's strong recent form (two wins from four in sim-going) and Harry Skelton's positional riding mean he could time a run to arrive late; he has the stamina for 2m7f and his headgear (bp) suggests he holds his concentration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses close the gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Smugglers Haven makes a critical jumping error, allowing hold-up types to close.
scenarios.body: Harrys Hope or Yes Day, despite being mapped to midfield out of their natural role, could benefit from a dramatic shift in race tempo; however, their redistribution away from the genuine rear means they are unlikely to be perfectly positioned to capitalise, limiting this scenario's probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank outsider springs surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes chaotic — multiple fallers or a badly-run race with a dramatic swing in pace — and a longer-priced runner finds the gaps.
scenarios.body: Palamon or King Roly, both hold-up types with unspectacular recent form, could steal into contention in a truly muddled race; Palamon's single win from 15 similar-going runs and King Roly's patchy 46-P29 form make this a low-conviction outcome.

watchPoints.text: Smugglers Haven jumping — if she makes a serious error at any of the final three fences she could hand the race to Muskerry Rock who will be travelling immediately behind her.

Harrys Hope and Yes Day are both genuine hold-up horses competing for the same rear-of-field ground; watch for interference or crowding between them in the early stages as neither can afford to lose more lengths if they are to make a meaningful late challenge.

King Roly's pulled-up run in his recent form (P in 46-P29) is unresolved — watch his jumping in the early-middle stages, as any sign of reluctance could see him pulled up again and disrupt those immediately behind.

Trainer Dan Skelton has two runners in this race (Palamon and Muskerry Rock) — watch for team tactics, specifically whether Palamon is used to press Smugglers Haven and soften her up for Muskerry Rock's late challenge.

races.name: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Turpin Gold
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a fine record on good ground (14/15 similar-going runs in the frame), handled over this kind of trip repeatedly, though Stan Sheppard will need Iolaos du Mou to set a real gallop to generate a closing chance.|
runners_data.comment: Turpin Gold arrives as our top-rated runner in this field and shaped with plenty of promise when a close third two starts back, giving encouragement he can go one better; carrying 168 lb after 49 days off is the main concern, though he has distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Definite Dream
runners_data.note: Brendan Powell's mount is the most natural prominent racer in the field apart from the leader, holding course form at this trip and appearing dependable on good going, though a run of five consecutive places without a win questions the finishing punch.|
runners_data.comment: Definite Dream has experience of today's trip and conditions, and her second three starts back gives her a solid claims profile that our rating of 99 supports; the chief concern is that she has been winless in recent starts, with a fifth last time out suggesting she needs to find improvement.

runners_data.name: Alshadhian
runners_data.note: Six-year-old carrying tongue tie and cheekpieces who has placed on similar going before, but his hold-up style means Jack Tudor will need a stronger pace than this race is likely to serve up, and he's only had 26 days since his last run.|

runners_data.name: Iolaos du Mou
runners_data.note: The sole genuine front-runner in the race; one win and course form over 16f on good going, and Tabitha Worsley can simply bowl along uncontested — the key question is whether his jumping holds up late over the full 2m½f trip.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out offers a clear positive for Iolaos du Mou, though two sixth-place finishes in between temper expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, and 26 days since his last start suggests he returns fresh, though 160 lb is a stiff burden to carry.

runners_data.name: Dexter
runners_data.note: Toby Wynne's mount wears a tongue tie, has shown decent placing form on good ground but is a natural hold-up horse who will find the congested midfield difficult to navigate — one of several Greenall/Guerriero-trained runners who needs things to go his way.|

runners_data.name: Greer Hill
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's five-year-old has top-speed form including a recent win, but is a genuine rearward racer forced into a midfield position by the volume of hold-up types in this field; William Shanahan (5) will struggle to find clear air if the closers bunch together.|
runners_data.comment: Greer Hill was a winner three starts back but has shown mixed form either side of it, including a pull-up and an eighth, with his third last time out at least a step back in the right direction; he has experience of today's trip and going, though 157 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Hiero Sport
runners_data.note: Kielan Woods partners a horse whose last win came over a similar trip on good ground at a patient, off-the-pace style, but 87 days off the track is a concern, and being drawn into a more prominent role than natural weakens his chance — the layoff compounds the fit.|
runners_data.comment: Hiero Sport won two starts back and was third last time out, showing consistency at this level, though 87 days off the track is a fitness query and his 153 lb burden is no gimme; has run over today's trip and going, which at least removes those unknowns.

runners_data.name: Mr McWhinny
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on good going and clearly has the form profile, but Jack Andrews' mount is a true hold-up operator who will not be at home racing forward in a contest where the rear ground is already claimed; the redistribution into midfield blunts his effectiveness.|
runners_data.comment: Mr McWhinny has winning form in recent starts, including a win last time out, and has run over today's trip and going, but ranked eighth of ten on our figures and lugging 151 lb, he looks up against it here.

runners_data.name: Keep Me Posted
runners_data.note: Harry Bannister takes the mount on a horse flagged as fading in finishes, with a poor recent form string including two pulled-up efforts; even in a scenario where late runners benefit, this nine-year-old's propensity to weaken makes it hard to see him involved.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two pulled-up efforts among them, Keep Me Posted is hard to fancy ranked ninth of ten on our figures; some familiarity with today's going is about the best that can be said for him here.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes partners the oldest runner in the field at 12, who has been extraordinarily consistent at placing (eight places from fifteen similar-going runs) but hasn't won in this grade; a natural hold-up horse in a race too congested at the rear for him to get a clean run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Getaway Jewel has been a persistent runner-up — second three of those occasions — yet ranked last on our figures here, making him hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Iolaos du Mou is the sole confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner handicap chase over 2m½f at Worcester, and with no genuine rival prepared to dispute the lead, Tabitha Worsley can dictate an uncontested, measured gallop from the front on good ground. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly made up of hold-up types — Greer Hill, Hiero Sport, Mr McWhinny, Keep Me Posted and Getaway Jewel are all natural rearward racers, with Turpin Gold, Dexter and Alshadhian also preferring to be covered up, leaving Definite Dream as the only legitimate prominent racer to push Iolaos du Mou for early position. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, meaning Greer Hill, Hiero Sport, Mr McWhinny and Getaway Jewel will be forced to race in closer proximity to the pace than suits them, with only the most naturally forward of these likely to actually settle in their preferred spot. This race shape — one honest front-runner, a genuine prominent racer in Definite Dream, and a congested midfield of closers who cannot all be delivered late — strongly favours the patient, prominent-to-lead profile that can control the fractions and repel rivals whose finishing kicks may be compromised by traffic or the lack of a true end-to-end test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iolaos Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Iolaos du Mou dictates an uncontested, sensible gallop and the hold-up battalion fails to close the gap on good ground.
scenarios.body: Iolaos du Mou has strong course form at Worcester and, untroubled on the front end, sets a rhythm that suits his jumping style; the closers, forced into untypical positions, never generate the momentum to reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Definite Dream tracks Iolaos du Mou throughout and uses his prominent position to hit the front approaching the last fence.
scenarios.body: Definite Dream is the natural second-in-command here and, with his going form solid on good turf, a tracking ride from Brendan Powell could see him overhaul the leader late without needing a searching pace test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Iolaos du Mou is strong enough to stretch the field and create a genuine closing opportunity for a rear-deployed runner.
scenarios.body: Turpin Gold is the most credentialled of the hold-up horses and has placed consistently over similar distances on good ground; Stan Sheppard's patient tactics could pay off if the gallop proves genuinely honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Breaks The Field
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a collapse in the pace sees multiple fallers or refusals, fundamentally reshaping the contest in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Hiero Sport and Mr McWhinny, both naturally suited to sitting off a strong pace and picking up late, could benefit if the race dissolves into a test of stamina and jumping accuracy rather than tactical positioning.

watchPoints.text: Iolaos du Mou's jumping under pressure — if he makes a significant error at any of the final three fences having controlled the race, the whole shape collapses and Definite Dream or Turpin Gold are immediate beneficiaries.

Traffic congestion in the midfield group — with Greer Hill, Hiero Sport, Mr McWhinny, Keep Me Posted and Getaway Jewel all forced closer to the pace than natural, interference or hampered runs are highly probable, particularly at the first fence and at the water jump.

Definite Dream's proximity to Iolaos du Mou — if Brendan Powell allows the leader to build too large a cushion through the back straight, Definite Dream may lack the finishing pace to bridge the gap on a good surface.

Hiero Sport's fitness after 87 days off — Alex Hales sends him out without a recent run and his best form has come fresh, but the redistribution into midfield means the layoff risk is amplified if he needs time to find his stride.

Greer Hill's trainer form (Jennie Candlish 4/10 in past 14 days) is the standout trainer angle in the race — if the five-year-old overcomes the style-fit penalty and finds a clear run, the in-form yard is worth noting.

races.name: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle Race (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Blue Topaz
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien runner returning after 279 days off, last win on good ground over 16f is directly relevant here, and prominent style suits a pace-pressed race — headgear worn, handles this going, but the long absence is a meaningful fitness query.

runners_data.name: Datstheholyallofit
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes the ride on this Patrick Neville-trained five-year-old who won on good ground over 16f last time and ran well twice at 17f on good; prominent racer with recent winning form who holds a realistic tactical chance pressed just behind the pace setters.

runners_data.name: Do Wah Diddy
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort at 16f on good but is flagged as fading in the finish, which is a concern in a race likely to be run at a true gallop; Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell (7lb claimer) takes the ride and the horse's best finish here was a second over this course and distance on good.

runners_data.name: Dreaming Of The Dr
runners_data.note: Luke Scott (3lb claimer) partners this unexposed type whose form reads seven-four-six, showing no wins or places on good ground in similar conditions; style is uncertain and the horse's recent 26-day turnaround at least confirms freshness, but the evidence of capability at this level is thin.

runners_data.name: Elated
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's five-year-old is a confirmed front-runner with a remarkably consistent record of placed finishes — 3-3-3-3-2 — but has never won a hurdle race; likely to push Sparkling Water from the off and the key question is whether she can outlast rivals rather than simply outpace them.

runners_data.name: Evenly
runners_data.note: Donald McCain entry with only one run on record, a sixth on good ground at 16f, making this a deeply lightly-raced horse with very little form to work with; Theo Gillard rides and the unknown profile makes this a significant risk in a competitive mares' maiden.

runners_data.name: Lady Bee Great
runners_data.note: Stan Sheppard for Matt Sheppard, a genuine hold-up horse whose recent form includes back-to-back wins but over flat/chase trips — the jump to 2m hurdles on good ground and the hold-up style in a pace-dominated race gives her the hardest task tactically.

runners_data.name: Nala The Lioness
runners_data.note: Form is predominantly over shorter on Flat/National Hunt Flat surfaces, including a placed effort at 13f on soft, suggesting both the hurdle trip and the good ground are significant unknowns; prominent style means she will be caught up in the early traffic battle, which may not suit her stamina profile.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Water
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners Dan Skelton's five-year-old, who has winning form at 16f on good ground most recently, and is the most likely pace-controller in this field; the Skelton handler-jockey combination at T14:2/5 suggests stable in form, and the horse's hold-up headgear note adds interest to whether she truly leads or settles early.

runners_data.name: Sweet Honey B
runners_data.note: Clive Boultbee-Brooks runner returning after 219 days away, with all form on soft ground — the step to good ground here is a genuine concern and the long layoff compounds the uncertainty; prominent style will place her in the firing line early but the going data suggests conditions may not suit.

runners_data.name: Whinny Houston
runners_data.note: Returning after a 420-day absence for Sheila Lewis, with a form string reading P-0 over hurdles — the long break, fade-in-finish flag, and thin form profile make this one of the more speculative entries in the race; Sean Houlihan rides.

runners_data.name: Matilda Maid
runners_data.note: Mrs Sara Bradstock's four-year-old has only one run, a tenth of ten on good at 16f, and carries a fades-in-finish flag alongside the lightest weight; Mr Daniel Williams (7lb claimer) aboard, and there is very little to suggest she can compete at the top of a field of this size.

runners_data.name: Pearl Knot
runners_data.note: Oliver Greenall and Josh Guerriero's four-year-old has form of U-5-8 over hurdles on good ground and unseated in her most recent start; Toby Wynne rides and the horse has shown limited ability to get competitive, though all runs have been at the right trip and going.

runners_data.name: Take The Boat
runners_data.note: Harry Bannister partners Georgina Nicholls' four-year-old, who is a genuine hold-up horse with a strong placed record (four placed from six runs on good); however, this horse has been mapped to midfield because the number of hold-up types in the rear exceeds what the race shape can accommodate — its natural deep-closing role is constrained by race dynamics, which tempers its realistic chance.

runners_data.name: Adba
runners_data.note: Harry Kimber for Faye Bramley, a three-year-old with one hurdle run (sixth on good at 16f) and flat form that includes consistent finishes outside the placings; age, inexperience, and limited form evidence make this the rawest entry in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Sparkling Water and Elated are the two confirmed front-runners in this 15-runner mares' maiden hurdle, and with both holding genuine early-pace intentions, a contested lead from the outset is virtually certain — Harry Skelton on Sparkling Water and Ben Jones on Elated are unlikely to yield without a fight, meaning the gallop should be honest to strong throughout the 2m trip on good ground at Worcester. Blue Topaz, Datstheholyallofit, Do Wah Diddy, and Nala The Lioness all carry prominent profiles and will be pressing close behind, creating a race with significant pace pressure across the first half. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Sparkling Water, trained and ridden by the Skelton yard at peak efficiency, is best placed to dominate on the front end, with Elated the most likely to push her, while Blue Topaz and Datstheholyallofit are the prominent runners most likely to actually latch onto the pace group. The contested pace and honest gallop on good ground over 2m at Worcester favours a resolute, prominent-to-lead profile with genuine stamina — horses that can race handy without burning out, rather than deep closers, are best positioned to capitalise as the field strings out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Strongest Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Sparkling Water dictates from Elated over the first mile and the honest gallop culls the field, the most durable prominent mover wins a stamina-driven finish.
scenarios.body: Sparkling Water attempts to control from the front with Elated pressing, and the pace gradually exposes weaknesses in the larger prominent group; whoever handles the rhythm best and jumps most cleanly enters the straight with a crucial advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Blowup, Midfield Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the Sparkling Water-Elated duel burns genuinely hot and both tire inside the final half-mile, a well-positioned midfield horse gets a clear run to the line.
scenarios.body: The frantic early exchanges leave the principals vulnerable late, handing an opportunity to any horse that has tracked in fourth or fifth without being involved in the battle; this suits runners who have shown the ability to pick up a tiring field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Elated Slips The Field
scenarios.trigger: If Elated dictates an uncontested or slightly steadier gallop and Sparkling Water is held up or blundered, a front-runner wins with a well-timed move from the prominent group.
scenarios.body: Elated's consistent placed form at this trip and on good ground makes her a credible pace-controlling winner if she avoids a brutal early duel; horses in the first three or four at the fourth flight have the best chance of going with her and sustaining a challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly relentless and the prominent group collectively fades, genuine hold-up horses may get into the argument in the final hurdle run-in.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely outcome given that Take The Boat and Lady Bee Great are true hold-up types in a field with heavy pace bias and at 2m the race may not be long enough for them to reel in a clear leader; however, a messy jumping incident or cavalry charge scenario could compress the race enough to give them a look.

watchPoints.text: Sparkling Water and Elated are on a collision course for the early lead — if either jumps poorly at the first or second hurdle, the other could steal an uncontested advantage that changes the entire race shape.

Take The Boat is a genuine hold-up horse mapped into midfield due to the volume of pace types in this race; punters should note it may be forced to race further forward than ideal, compromising its natural finishing style.

Sweet Honey B has all her form on soft ground and returns from 219 days off — if the good ground is faster than she handles, she could fade abruptly after the halfway point and cause interference in the closely-grouped prominent pack.

Blue Topaz makes her first appearance in 279 days — watch her in the paddock and early in the race for signs of rustiness, as Fergal O'Brien horses can need a run back but the form on return is worth monitoring.

Whinny Houston is absent 420 days with a poor prior form record — flag for safety in a 15-runner field over hurdles where an out-of-form, long-absent runner jumping inexpertly creates risk for those racing close behind.

races.paceDynamic: Newbrook Diamond and Oneinthewell are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the gates, with Newbrook Diamond (blinkers, Sean Bowen, Gordon Elliott) likely to assert given the superior OR and stronger recent form, while Oneinthewell (cheekpieces, Jonathan Burke) will not be surrendering that position without a fight. Behind them, Road To Wembley, Square d'Alboni, Handmedownastar, Phantom Gold, and Likewhatyousee all want prominent berths in a 12-runner field, creating significant early congestion and a real risk of traffic problems between the second-last and last flights. The resulting pace — honest but not suicidal on Good ground — should be consistent enough to stretch the field out and avoid a falsely-run crawl, which is exactly the scenario that suits the horse who can sit just off the pace in a clean position, travel without burning resources in the early skirmish, and produce a sustained one-pace gallop home rather than a sharp sprint. The tactical verdict is clear: genuine hold-up horses and those able to sit second or third without fighting for position are best placed, while the two front-runners face the risk of running each other into the ground for the benefit of closers tracking from the outside.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Newbrook Diamond and Oneinthewell set a genuine pace that strings the field out from the third-last, allowing a prominent tracker to cruise into the lead from two out.
scenarios.body: The consistent early tempo burns off the two lead-fighting front-runners in the straight, and a horse who has settled just behind the scrimmage in third or fourth — covering ground efficiently — pounces at the second-last with energy to spare; on Good ground at Worcester, stamina at this 2m4f trip rewards those who race within themselves early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Newbrook Diamond successfully shakes off Oneinthewell by the halfway point and establishes a controlled solo lead, dictating a measured gallop.
scenarios.body: With blinkers on and Bowen in the saddle for Elliott, Newbrook Diamond has the class (OR 126, two recent wins on Good) and profile to settle into a rhythm once the inter-front-runner duel is resolved, and a well-judged solo display on a track that does not over-penalise front-runners on Good ground could see it hold on comfortably.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace between Newbrook Diamond and Oneinthewell becomes genuinely fierce and the race falls apart at the third-last, leaving late ground to be made up.
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start collapse of the front-running duel could open a gap for hold-up horses who have been tracking patiently through the field; Shesonnet (recent Good-ground form, 2-2-2 frame) and Not Now (prominent in running, strong track profile) are best positioned to sweep past a tiring pack from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Congestion Derails Fancied
scenarios.trigger: If the five-strong prominent cluster causes interference between the 3rd-last and 2nd-last hurdles, forcing jockeys wide or into checking movements.
scenarios.body: A chaotic mid-race traffic incident could eliminate fancied prominent types and open the race to unexpected winners emerging from deeper cover; horses drawn with cleaner runs on the outside become beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Newbrook Diamond and Oneinthewell will fight for the lead from the first hurdle — watch for either horse being sent wide or quickening sharply off the bend as Bowen and Burke contest supremacy, which could cause a concertina effect through the prominent group behind them.

The five prominent-style runners (Road To Wembley, Square d'Alboni, Handmedownastar, Phantom Gold, Likewhatyousee) all want similar early positions in a 12-runner field — a traffic pile-up or checking movement between the 3rd-last and 2nd-last hurdles is a real risk for the tightly-grouped mid-section.

Cadillac Ranch — 135 days off, amateur rider, no Going data, lightly raced — is a genuine wild card in a contested early pace; watch for it being outpaced early or jumping erratically and interfering with horses around it.

Handmedownastar returns after 87 days off but has a perfect Going profile and minimal exposed form; watch how quickly it travels in the first mile as a guide to whether the layoff has left it short or fresh and primed.

Shesonnet is the hold-up runner with the most specific course-relevant form at 2m4f on Good — watch its position at the top of the straight as a proxy for whether the pace has genuinely been contested enough to set up late closers.

races.name: CopyBet Follow Us On X Handicap Hurdle Race (Div I)

runners_data.name: Starshine Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Olly Murphy and Sean Bowen, decent sim-going form (5 wins/places from 12), but recent efforts show finishes of 3-5-7 with no win since bumper days — needs a truly run race at 2m4f to get competitive from the rear, which the contested pace could theoretically provide.
runners_data.comment: Starshine Legend showed real promise when third three starts back, and returns here fresh on 28 days' rest with going experience in his favour; the concern is he has been winless since, with a seventh last time out suggesting he may need to find more.

runners_data.name: Midnight Jewel
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Charlie Longsdon, strong sim-going profile (12/15) and a win over this exact trip on Good ground in recent history — the 10-year-old carries 164lbs but has the front-running profile to set and potentially steal this race if Gone In Sixty weakens early.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Jewel shaped with promise when third five starts back and struck gold four starts back, but two pulled-up efforts since cloud his recent record; he returns after 28 days and has run over today's trip and going, with a rating of 104 making him the one to beat on paper.

runners_data.name: Mrs Biddle
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing mare for Harry Cobden and Kayley Woollacott, returning from a lengthy 284-day absence which is the main query — two solid Good-ground runs in her history (including a second over 20f) suggest she retains the class, but the layoff means fitness must be taken on trust.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, and 284 days off the track is a significant fitness query for Mrs Biddle, though a second two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer some encouragement; 160 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Iamcelestialgift
runners_data.note: Prominent type with strong sim-going numbers (5 from 6 on Good), fitted with a tongue-tie, and drops from OR 88 which is competitive here — the 8-year-old's recent form string of 69 after a pull-up is inconsistent but Good ground form is credible and Nick Slatter's 3lb claim is useful.
runners_data.comment: Iamcelestialgift has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 97 puts him clear of his official mark, suggesting he holds strong claims at his best — yet a pulled-up run recently and a winless recent spell make him hard to trust fully.

runners_data.name: Warner's Cross
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a recent win over 20f on Good and strong sim-going stats (10/15, 2 wins) — the headgear note (h) and Harry Reed partnership is worth noting, and from 24 days off he arrives fresh, making him the standout candidate if the pace truly breaks the field up.
runners_data.comment: Warner's Cross won last time out and returns on a quick turnaround of 24 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour; however, two pulled-up efforts in recent starts raise durability questions, and 156 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner for Alex Hales and Kielan Woods, with an exceptional sim-going profile (14/15) and multiple placings over 20f on Good — the key tactical question is whether he can hold off Midnight Jewel's challenge early or whether they exhaust each other, which most likely benefits those just behind.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Gone In Sixty faces a stiff task here, though he does come into this fresh enough at 28 days between runs and has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Could Be You
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Neil Mulholland, but the trainer's 0/6 run in the last 14 days is a significant concern, and the 120-day break combined with a warning flag for fading in the finish makes this a horse to treat with caution — sim-going record of just 1/5 on Good underlines the worry.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — including two pulled-up efforts — and rated lowest in the field on our figures, Could Be You is hard to fancy here; 120 days off adds another question mark, though he has run over today's trip and carries a workable 150 lb.

runners_data.name: Dynamite Defense
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies' 5-year-old has genuine hold-up tendencies in his natural racing, but with multiple hold-up types in this field he is unlikely to secure his preferred rear position — his recent third over 20f on Good is the best piece of form, though racing out of his natural role reduces confidence in a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and carrying 148 lb, Dynamite Defense does bring experience over today's trip and going, and that third last time out shows he can threaten, though 49 days off the track and a ranking of sixth of ten leave questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Babychino
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old for Alexander Gibbons carrying bottom weight of 144lbs, ridden by Sophie Carter (7lb claim), with decent recent form including a second over 22f on Good — the youth and low weight are assets in a stamina test, though the amateur claim and limited experience over hurdles at this level are checks.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Babychino is hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and shaped with some promise, finishing second and third in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Lucky In Taipan
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's 6-year-old is a natural hold-up horse who, like Dynamite Defense, is unlikely to find clear passage from the rear given how many similar types populate this field — six from eight sim-going runs place him in midfield on form, but a record of 0 wins and just 1 place from hold-up racing suggests limited upside even if the run goes smoothly.
runners_data.comment: Rated well clear of his official mark at 100, Lucky In Taipan shapes as a leading threat carrying 142 lb, and has run over today's going before; the main concern is that he is winless in his last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Jewel and Gone In Sixty are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 2m4f trip on Good ground at Worcester, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a dawdle. That honest, competitive pace is set from the first flight and is unlikely to relent, meaning the race will be run at a consistent tempo with neither leader able to fully dictate on their own terms. The sustained gallop over an extended trip on quick ground favours horses that can travel smoothly in behind the pace and pick up in the latter stages — the prominent-to-midfield profile, specifically types like Mrs Biddle and Iamcelestialgift who can sit just off a genuine pace, are best placed. Dynamite Defense and Lucky In Taipan are genuine hold-up horses squeezed into a midfield mapping because this field holds more true rear-runners than the race shape has room to accommodate at the back — of the two confirmed leaders, Midnight Jewel has the stronger front-running profile at this trip and is more likely to secure the rail and set the terms.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Jewel and Gone In Sixty lock horns from the start, setting a genuine honest gallop that suits a horse travelling prominently just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other off over 2m4f on Good ground, and a horse settled just behind them — tracking the tempo without expending early energy — arrives with a clean run to the last and has enough in reserve to power home. Mrs Biddle and Iamcelestialgift are the profile fits, able to track the leaders and capitalise on the contested front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Gone In Sixty or Midnight Jewel breaks clear unchallenged early or one of the pair weakens, leaving the other to dictate at a controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: A sole front-runner finds the race set up perfectly to their strengths, dictating at a pace that suits their stamina and never letting rivals get competitive enough to threaten. Midnight Jewel's strong hurdle record at this trip on Good ground and sim-going form (12/15) makes them the more credible candidate to steal a march if Gone In Sixty capitulates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is genuinely strong enough to stop the prominent horses, creating a truly run race where stamina and a late run become the decisive factors.
scenarios.body: Warner's Cross, who won over 20f on Good recently and is a proven hold-up type with strong sim-going stats, would be the principal beneficiary, sweeping past a tiring field from the back of midfield. Starshine Legend also fits this profile though form consistency has been mixed, and the pace would need to be truly searching to allow hold-up horses to land this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners cancel each other out quickly and the race falls into a muddling, falsely-run gallop with multiple horses vying for position mid-race.
scenarios.body: A messy pace scenario scrambles the form book and hands an advantage to the horse with the best turn of foot late on regardless of running style, favouring unexposed or lightly weighted horses with a finishing kick. Babychino, a young 4-year-old carrying bottom weight, and Could Be You, if returning with improvement after 120 days off, are the principal dangers in this unlikely but possible scenario.

watchPoints.text: Midnight Jewel and Gone In Sixty — watch the first half-mile closely; if neither gives way and they drive hard at each other from flag-fall, both risk emptying before the second-last and the entire race shape tilts toward prominent hold-up types.

Mrs Biddle — Harry Cobden accepts the ride despite the 284-day layoff, which is a significant positive, but watch for any signs of greenness or blowing hard after the race that might indicate she needed this run rather than winning off it.

Warner's Cross — a genuine hold-up performer in a race with a compressed midfield; watch whether Harry Reed can find a clean passage around the final turn, because traffic trouble is a real risk given how many horses are bunched in similar positions.

Could Be You — the 120-day absence and trainer's cold 14-day strike rate (0/6) make him a horse to monitor in the market; any significant late support would deserve attention, but on public form and fitness grounds he is treated cautiously until proven otherwise.

Dynamite Defense and Lucky In Taipan — both are natural hold-up horses mapped into midfield through redistribution; watch whether either jockey (James Best, Ben Jones) opts to drop them out regardless, which would tell you they are conceding position entirely and relying on the pace burning itself out completely.

runners_data.name: Bannister
runners_data.note: Best form in similar going (1W4P on Good in recent history); Tom Broughton claiming 3lb is a useful allowance, and this 9yo has enough staying stamina to reward a patient ride if the front-runners tire — his natural hold-up style suits a truly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Bannister is winless in his last five starts, but that second-placed effort five starts back and a solid profile over today's trip and going make him a genuine threat from 168 lb, with his weight the main concern.

runners_data.name: Bound For Glory
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner in the field; 4yo lightly weighted and handles Good ground well with a win at this distance, though trainer is 0/3 over 14 days and the style-fit tag notes he is racing slightly out of role on this map — he is, however, squarely in his natural position here.
runners_data.comment: Bound For Glory shaped well when third two starts back and landed a win three starts back, showing he retains ability; fit on a 28-day break and with experience of today's going, the 166 lb burden is the main query.

runners_data.name: Crafty Gael
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over on this 7yo, who wears a tongue-tie and has a modest recent strike-rate on similar ground (0W6P); trips of 19-20f have been his habitat but form has been flat and he may need things to go wrong for others.
runners_data.comment: Crafty Gael was placed third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims as a leading danger here; the main concern is a winless run in his last four starts that suggests the weight of 163 lb may just find him out.

runners_data.name: Royal Rhythm
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill have hit 1/5 over the last 14 days which is modest; this 10yo wears a hood and is 0W3P on Good ground in recent starts, but his prominent style means he won't be far away and he's the most natural challenger to the leader.
runners_data.comment: Royal Rhythm has run over today's trip and going, returns after 34 days looking fresh, and his third last time out suggests ability worth respecting at this level, with our rating of 85 making him a solid threat; however, two pulled-up efforts in recent starts are a concern.

runners_data.name: Usyk
runners_data.note: Five-year-old ridden by a 7lb claimer (Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell), returning after 38 days; form of 3-4-5 on Good ground at shorter trips suggests he handles the surface, but stepping to 2m4f is a question mark for a horse with no wins yet recorded.

runners_data.name: Boskill Borden
runners_data.note: David Rees runner who wears a visor; a genuine hold-up horse whose true inclination is to race from the rear — pushed onto the map in midfield purely because of the field's back-heavy density, and the style-fit flag means his chance may be overstated in any scenario requiring early positioning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up last time out, Boskill Borden faces an uphill task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and 28 days off may have freshened him; the 154 lb burden is no help.

runners_data.name: Onehundredneighty
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's 6yo returns after a 91-day break, the longest absence in the field, which is a fitness question; best form has come on Soft ground (2nd, 3rd) and the Good surface brings only 0W0P in eight similar-going runs — naturally a hold-up horse shuffled forward on the map.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Onehundredneighty returns after a 91-day absence carrying 152 lb, with a third three starts back the only crumb of comfort in a moderate recent record.

runners_data.name: Ghost Jury
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden adds significant jockey quality at OR=76, and Ghost Jury has placed twice in Good-ground races at 2m2f-2m6f; however, his true back-of-the-field style means he will likely be racing from further back than his map position suggests, needing a strong pace to bring him into play.
runners_data.comment: Ghost Jury showed up with a second last time out and did score once in her last five, but ranked seventh of nine on our figures she faces a stiff task here, and 150 lb is a significant burden after 47 days off.

runners_data.name: Brooklyn Lullaby
runners_data.note: The Easterby yard has been busy (3/33 over 14 days); this 6yo has shaped prominently when placed and has Good-ground form at shorter trips — stepping to 2m4f is new territory but the prominent style gives him a tactical edge over the hold-up brigade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and a little light on recent racecourse action after 50 days off, Brooklyn Lullaby at least showed renewed spirit with a second last time out, and has run over today's going before, giving her a fair each-way squeak from a rating of 72.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Spirit
runners_data.note: A 4yo carrying bottom weight with a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag — consistent record of finishing out of the frame (0809-0 recent form) on both Good and Soft ground; wears hood and tongue-tie and is the highest-risk runner in the field, genuinely mapped forward when his instinct is to race from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Cosmic Spirit is lightly raced and unexposed, yet to win in recent starts, though returning after 64 days carries a fitness question under 142 lb; still open to improvement as his true ceiling remains to be seen.

races.paceDynamic: Bound For Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap hurdle over 2m4f at Worcester on Good ground, and with no genuine pace rival to push him, he is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled tempo from the front. Royal Rhythm and Brooklyn Lullaby will look to track him in the prominent positions, meaning the early sections should be orderly rather than pressured. This measured pace over the trip on a fair surface is likely to set up a thorough stamina test rather than a sprint finish, which plays into the hands of horses who travel well within themselves before picking up — a prominent-to-midfield profile that can sustain its effort through the final two flights rather than a pure come-from-behind type. A significant number of hold-up horses — Boskill Borden, Onehundredneighty, Ghost Jury, and Cosmic Spirit — have been redistributed forward on the map because the field is genuinely back-heavy, but in practice they will fill the rear; Bound For Glory and Royal Rhythm are the runners most likely to actually secure early position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bound For Glory Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bound For Glory dictates a calm, uncontested tempo and reaches the final flight with his rivals struggling to close.
scenarios.body: Allowed to roll along at his own pace, Bound For Glory can exploit his front-running comfort zone over this 2m4f trip on Ground that suits him, and with no rival willing or able to seriously pressure him early, he reaches the home turn with enough in reserve to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and a close tracker pounces between the last two flights.
scenarios.body: Royal Rhythm or Brooklyn Lullaby, sitting just off the leader throughout, can capitalise if Bound For Glory's effort flattens out in the closing stages, with the stamina of a prominent traveller proving decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Produces Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to take the edge off the front pair and a hold-up horse with genuine staying power comes through.
scenarios.body: Bannister, operating from further back on a course and going combination he handles, is the best-credentialled true hold-up runner in the field and could emerge late if the leaders empty; Usyk, also dropping back in trip relative to recent runs, is another who could pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Movers Outrun Ratings
scenarios.trigger: If the race evolves chaotically — leaders stop, hold-up horses are outpaced, and a lower-rated runner finds clear sailing.
scenarios.body: Ghost Jury, who has placed twice over this sort of trip on Good ground and is ridden by Harry Cobden, could outrun his OR=76 mark if a muddled finish suits a horse with course-applicable form; Onehundredneighty's best efforts have come in similarly unpredictable races.

watchPoints.text: Watch Bound For Glory's jumping — if he makes a serious error at any of the early hurdles, the controlling pace disappears entirely and the race becomes genuinely open for Royal Rhythm to capitalise.
Harry Cobden on Ghost Jury is a significant booking upgrade at OR=76 — if Cobden pushes him closer than his natural hold-up style would suggest, Ghost Jury could outrun his odds in a muddled finish.

Onehundredneighty's 91-day absence is the longest in the race; watch the market moves close to post time — any significant support for Ben Pauling's runner despite the layoff would suggest confidence from connections.

The entire field except Bound For Glory and Royal Rhythm is inclined to race from midfield or further back — if anything robs the race of its only genuine front-runner early, there is no natural pace replacement and the tempo could collapse unpredictably.

Brooklyn Lullaby's step up to 2m4f (previous best trip 2m2f) is untested — if the extra distance finds him out, the Easterby yard's 3/33 recent strike-rate offers limited confidence that he'll see the trip out.

runners_data.name: Back In The Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won and placed repeatedly on Good ground; OR 104 and lightly-raced at 2m7f is a stamina query, but James Owen's runner will look to exploit a lead from flag-fall and may find the six-way pace battle more competitive than he'd like.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner four starts back, Back In The Bay returns after 43 days off carrying a hefty 168 lb, which is the chief concern; she has going experience in her favour but her last two starts have yielded only a fifth and a seventh.

runners_data.name: October Hill
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse returning just four days after last run — the short turnaround under David Pipe is notable and could blunt his finishing effort, though a win and a second over 2m on Good ground shows ability; tongue-strap fitted.

runners_data.name: Fiskardo
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Mickey Bowen who has been stepping up in trip (form suggests he thrives over shorter), making the jump to 2m7f a significant stamina test; Shane Fenelon (5) rides and the tongue-strap was fitted last time — pace duel with Back In The Bay likely to be costly.
runners_data.comment: Fiskardo arrives in solid recent form — second three starts back and a winner four starts back — and returns after 24 days on going he has encountered before, with a rating of 103 backing his claims; the concern is a fourth last time out suggesting he may just be coming off the boil.

runners_data.name: Mistral Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Fergal O'Brien with a solid record over 2m4f on Good ground; three wins from 15 runs in similar conditions and the eight-year-old has the profile of a solid each-way player without the finishing zip to dominate from the front — Fern O'Brien (5) takes 5lbs off.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 16 on our figures and finishing sixth last time out, Mistral Blue is hard to fancy at the weights, though a win two starts back and experience over today's distance and going offer some crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Betty's Tiara
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has consistently finished in the 7th-9th range over similar trips and conditions over the past season — recent form offers little encouragement for a bold show even if she leads; tongue and bit headgear fitted.
runners_data.comment: Betty's Tiara rates as the pick of the field on our figures, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but winless in her last five starts and a string of finishes no better than fourth make the burden of 164 lb a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Redbridge Rambler
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the Keighley yard who won over 2m4f Good 32 days ago and has 12 of 15 runs on similar going — the step up to 2m7f is the key question, but the consistent second-placed finishes (4/4) suggest he stays well enough and Freddie Keighley (5) claims 5lbs.
runners_data.comment: Redbridge Rambler won three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but a fifth and fourth since suggest he has found life tougher lately; the 163 lb burden is no help, though a 32-day break could see him sharper here.

runners_data.name: Stiletto
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who was a course winner over 2m3f on Good just 40 days ago under Harry Cobden — the top jockey booking is the headline angle and Cobden's ability to position from off the pace in a fast-run race makes Stiletto a live closer, with headgear (p) for focus.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 16 on our figures and carrying a hefty 163 lb, Stiletto is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, but that sole recent victory sits amid a largely disappointing run of form.

runners_data.name: Final Entry
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for David Pipe who won over 2m6f Good and was placed twice over 2m6f — the 2m7f trip looks well within range; tongue and visor combination fitted, and Jack Tudor takes the ride with good course awareness.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 16 on our figures, Final Entry makes a tough ask, and he was only fourth latest; the win came two starts back, though he does bring distance and going experience and returns on a manageable 34-day break.

runners_data.name: Atreides
runners_data.note: Prominent type without a win in 15 Good-ground outings — consistent placings (four times) suggest he keeps galloping but lacks the decisive effort to win; visor and tongue-strap fitted, and the amateur rider (10lb claim) partially offsets the weight.
runners_data.comment: Atreides has shown consistent placing ability, with a third last time out and a second five starts back, but he remains winless in recent starts and his 162 lb burden looks a stiff ask for a gelding rated 98 returning after 34 days off.

runners_data.name: Kenzo Des Bruyeres
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has been pulled up last time and has no wins in six Good-ground starts — the visor is fitted but recent form over 2m4f-2m6f is uninspiring; James Bowen's booking suggests connections are hopeful, but the evidence is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 16 on our figures, Kenzo Des Bruyeres is hard to fancy, with a pulled-up effort last time out his most recent calling card; he has run over today's going before, and 26 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Barry Fife
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has placed three times on Good ground without winning over 2m3f-2m4f — the visor is fitted and Sam Twiston-Davies is a quality booking, but Barry Fife at OR 97 has not convinced over marathon distances and the pull-up last run is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Barry Fife at least offers the consolation of distance and going experience, and 28 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a pull-up two starts back and a hefty 161 lb to carry are notable negatives for a horse ranked sixth of sixteen.

runners_data.name: The Great Escape
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won over 2m3f Good 34 days ago for Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill (trainer 14-day strike 1/5) — the step up to 2m7f is significant for a horse who has won over 2m3f; Richie McLernon rides and the recent win gives confidence, though stamina over the extra distance is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to winning form last time out and returns after a 34-day break in good order, having run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 160 lb is the main test, but on the strength of that recent victory he makes plenty of appeal at a rating of 105.

runners_data.name: Mancero
runners_data.note: Prominent four-year-old for David Pipe with a strong recent record — two wins and a second from five Good-ground starts, including a win at 2m3f just 28 days ago; the cheekpieces are fitted and Sean Bowen's booking for the lightest horse in the field (156lbs) gives real pace-map appeal if he can travel off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below his official mark on our figures and among the outsiders in this field, Mancero does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but a pulled-up effort two starts back makes his jumping reliability hard to fully trust.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Charlie Longsdon who has three placed efforts over 2m3f-2m4f on Good ground — David Bass takes the ride but the form string (P3 recently) shows a horse who struggles to see out stamina-testing trips; 12 of 15 runs on similar going is a positive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but has placed three times in that sequence, including a third last time out 34 days ago; Ikigai Star has run over today's trip and going, though 155 lb is a stern burden and that pulled-up effort two starts back is a concern.

runners_data.name: Farhh Echo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 122 days off — the long absence combined with a form string of 0P880- on Good ground and an historical tendency to fade in the finish makes this one of the hardest to trust; tongue-strap and headgear fitted, and Liam Harrison's booking offers little compensating angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up three runs back, Farhh Echo has questions to answer, though he has experience of today's going and a rating of 98 suggests he holds more ability than his recent efforts have shown after 122 days off.

runners_data.name: Sims' Law
runners_data.note: A genuine back-marker by nature — mapped to midfield here only because the field holds more true hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; OR 68 and a form string of P9P-0 with no wins in four same-going starts means racing out of role simply compounds already limited evidence of ability.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Sims' Law is yet to win in his last four starts but has shown enough in glimpses to remain of interest; returning after 67 days off carrying 142 lb, he is one to watch as he continues to develop.

races.paceDynamic: Back In The Bay, Fiskardo, Betty's Tiara, The Great Escape, Kenzo Des Bruyeres, and Ikigai Star all carry confirmed front-running profiles, making a strong, honest gallop over 2m7f on Good ground virtually certain from the outset. With six genuine lead types in a 17-runner field, several will be unable to secure their natural position and will either burn energy disputing or be forced to drop back, effectively thinning the field from the front and setting up a stamina examination in the closing stages. The field also holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear, with Sims' Law redistributed to midfield despite being a genuine back-marker — its chance in any shape dependent on ground covered from behind is materially discounted. This race shape strongly favours genuine, proven stayers who can race prominently but off the pace — horses like Cinnodin, Redbridge Rambler, and Mancero who can sit just behind the scrimmage, let the speed-duel in front play out, and still find a change of gear at the business end of 2m7f on testing Good turf.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Aids Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If Back In The Bay, Fiskardo, and Betty's Tiara fight for lead, setting a searching tempo that burns out the front rank by the final climb.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will drain the genuine front-runners and leave the race to hold-prominent types sitting three to five lengths off the pace, cruising into contention from the third-last hurdle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If one of Back In The Bay or Fiskardo dominates early and settles into a controlled rhythm, reducing the pace pressure on the leaders.
scenarios.body: A steadier tempo favours the front-runner who leads alone and has the stamina to see it out over 2m7f, with only a small margin for those in behind to reel them in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns so fiercely that even prominent-runners are compromised and the race falls apart in the straight, leaving room for hold-up horses to mop up.
scenarios.body: Stiletto and Final Entry, who race from rear-to-midfield and possess good finishing form on Good ground, could pick up the pieces if the leaders have emptied; October Hill's recent second gives hope but the short turnaround from 4 days is a risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Moderate Test
scenarios.trigger: If several front-runners refuse to go on and the field crawls in the early stages, producing a tactical contest rather than a stamina test.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run 2m7f would bring hold-up horses and high-cruising-speed types into play, though few in this field have the quick-fire turn of foot to dominate a sprint finish over hurdles.

watchPoints.text: Back In The Bay, Fiskardo, Betty's Tiara, Kenzo Des Bruyeres, and Ikigai Star are all confirmed front-runners — watch the opening quarter-mile for a fierce pace duel that could burn out most of them and leave the race to those tracking from prominent midfield.

Cinnodin is stepping up to a career-high trip (2m7f) having won over 2m at Worcester 57 days ago — watch whether Gavin Sheehan settles him smoothly in the prominent position, as the extra ground in a fast-run race is the key test of his claims.

October Hill runs just four days after his last start — watch his movement through the race from the early stages as any sign of fatigue or stiffness under Rian Corcoran could see him drop away before the final flight despite his placed form.

The Great Escape is unproven beyond 2m3f — watch whether Richie McLernon attempts to control from the front or sits in behind, as the 2m7f distance on Good is untested ground and the stamina query is live.

Sims' Law is running off OR 68 in a field where the pace map has redistributed it to midfield — watch if Benjamin Macey (5) attempts to get cover at the rear as the horse's natural style and limited recent form make any prominent role in the race shape unlikely to be sustained.
